a_verdict_flips.statement: No recorded accept/stop verdict flips. Every change is interval-level only, and in each case a point-estimate threshold or a negative point estimate still decides the registered rule. The sealed window carries no verdict artifact at all, so its statistical leg flips from 'straddles zero' to 'strictly positive' without overturning a recorded decision.

b_masked_significance.statement: Yes: these comparisons were reported as indistinguishable from zero only because the archived interval was ~4.5x too wide. Under the corrected caliber the same point estimate is strictly positive with a lower bound above zero. The registered rule still says stop where a 0.003 threshold or the sign of the estimate blocks it, but the evidence is no longer 'no effect'.

c_threshold_gated.statement: Five judgments are decided by a threshold or a sign, not by interval width, so the caliber fix cannot move them: C1 fails the point leg 0.0014 < 0.0017; the 927 extension needs a positive delta and its delta is -0.00046; feature norm at 1.32 (+0.00167), 2.64 (-0.00007) and the extension batch (-0.00001) all fail the 0.003 point floor. A further seven judgments never carried the bug at all, because their builders already resampled ceil(n/5) blocks or period blocks (the six dose-curve rows and the promotion gate, plus C1 which is listed above because its point leg already decides it): for those the archived interval is reproduced bit-for-bit. Only two rows keep a live interval question: the sealed-window measurement, whose statistical leg flips from straddling zero to strictly positive (and which has no verdict artifact to flip), and feature norm at 1.32, whose interval flips positive but still cannot clear the 0.003 threshold.

multiplicity: The 8 candidate comparisons in runs/mbb-caliber-20261028/recompute.json plus the 13 archived judgments re-judged here (six judgment families: dose, C1, 927 extension, promotion gate, feature norm, sealed) are 21 paired comparisons selected on the same five development windows and the same 104 trading days, all of them after seeing the scores, with no multiplicity correction. The intervals that change are still increments of +0.0009 to +0.0016 in RankIC at most, i.e. 1.1%-2.0% of the 0.0788 candidate level: a caliber correction, not a new effect. Read the corrections as 'the same estimate was always positive', not as 'a new finding survived a stricter family-wise bar'.
conclusion: The caliber bug is real but local. It never touched the dose-curve builder, the C1 builder or the promotion gate, which had their own correct ceil(n/5) estimators (the dose builder even documents the single-block bug). It did inflate the rung-compare, featnorm, 927-extension and sealed intervals by ~4.5x. Correcting them turns several 'not distinguishable from zero' readings into strictly positive ones, but no registered accept/stop verdict changes, because every one of those verdicts is decided by a point-estimate threshold (0.003 / 0.0034) or by a negative point estimate.
